@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@
+# CiFn durable remote shell execution checkpoint
+
+2026-10-20. Adds a functioning remote shell runner to the durable control plane.
+It supersedes the root-only/no-completion limits in the earlier dispatch
+checkpoint for newly prepared runs. Production readiness remains incomplete.
+
+## Protocol and durable state
+
+All jobs now have an encrypted prepared payload captured at run acceptance.
+Root intents start ready; dependent intents start blocked. Their environment and
+secret snapshot is retained rather than reconstructed or re-resolved when a
+predecessor completes.
+
+The existing authenticated heartbeat offers a durable claim. Three bounded JSON
+endpoints use the registered runner secret, not an application API key:
+
+- `POST /api/v1/runners/claims/resume`: `runnerId`, optional pagination cursor.
+  Returns only that runner's outstanding claims and their prepared payloads.
+- `POST /api/v1/runners/claims/ack`: `runnerId`, `runId`, `dispatchId`,
+  `claimToken`, `executionId`. CAS binds an execution identity before work starts.
+  Repeating the same acknowledgement is safe; competing identities conflict.
+- `POST /api/v1/runners/claims/complete`: the same identity plus `result` with a
+  terminal job status and the exact ordered step keys/terminal statuses.
+
+Completion requires the runner binding, claim token and acknowledged execution
+identity. Invalid authentication returns 401, malformed shape 400, stale or
+conflicting identity/result 409, and a storage failure 503. Server-observed
+completion timestamps are assigned internally. A canonical result digest makes
+identical retries return the same `{accepted:true}` receipt without applying a
+second transition; a conflicting result is rejected.
+
+One run-row CAS commits completion, step/job statuses, dependent-intent promotion
+and the resulting run status. An already ready/claimed/completed intent cannot
+be scheduled again. Concurrent parent completions can release a join only once.
+Failed dependencies skip blocked descendants; independent branches may finish.
+A run becomes terminal only when all jobs are terminal. Cancelled runs reject
+new execution acknowledgements and completions that were not already committed.
+Notifications are not made durable by this transition.
+
+The payload's `dispatchProtocolVersion:2` marks fully prepared runs. Earlier
+record-only or root-only payloads remain readable but are not automatically
+published/claimed by this execution protocol. Old claims without protocol
+metadata are reconciliation-only. There is no automatic migration or unsafe
+secret re-resolution for historical records; reconcile them explicitly before
+creating replacement work.
+
+## Runner lifecycle and secret handling
+
+The built runner requires `CIFN_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, `CIFN_RUNNER_ID`,
+`CIFN_RUNNER_SECRET` and an explicit persistent `CIFN_RUNNER_STATE_DIR`.
+`CIFN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` defaults to 1000 (minimum 10). The control plane must use
+the durable SQLite store for these endpoints. MemoryStore remains available for
+local execution, not remote durability.
+
+The runner reuses the existing Runner and shell executor with an ephemeral
+per-job projection. That projection drives actual subprocess execution and
+collects results; it is not the durable authority. Only shell `run` steps are
+supported by this remote checkpoint. Image/container jobs and provider `uses`
+steps fail explicitly. Existing local execution/provider paths remain available
+and separately tested.
+
+Before acknowledging a claim, the runner saves only identity/execution metadata
+in its journal. It fsyncs an exclusive started marker before invoking the shell,
+then durably saves terminal statuses before sending completion. Journal files
+use mode 0600, the directory mode 0700, atomic replacement and directory fsync.
+The journal contains no raw job environment, commands, log output, provider
+credentials or runner secret. It retains scoped claim/execution tokens and
+terminal statuses. Resume re-fetches payloads through runner authentication.
+
+On restart:
+
+- Unacknowledged offers and prepared journal entries may be resumed.
+- A saved completed result is resent, never re-executed. A permanent conflict or
+  invalid result is retained in reconciliation state without blocking later jobs.
+- A started marker without a saved result is uncertain. The runner emits a
+  generic reconciliation diagnostic and refuses automatic re-execution.
+- An execution acknowledged elsewhere cannot be adopted with a new identity.
+
+The exclusive started marker also prevents two local processes using one journal
+from spawning the same execution. This protects against duplicate execution
+caused by protocol/journal retries; it does not claim exactly-once external side
+effects or recover an unknown result after a process/host loss.
+
+Full-job logging was removed. Shell jobs receive prepared job variables plus a
+small base environment (PATH/LANG/TMPDIR), not the runner's control-plane
+credentials. Results saved/reported by this path contain statuses only, so raw
+stdout/stderr and secret values cannot enter the journal. Existing executor
+redaction is retained for its in-memory logs. This is not an OS/container sandbox.
+
+## Validation
+
+Real SQLite protocol tests exercise owner/runner/token binding, acknowledgement
+retries, competing execution owners, wrong step results, duplicate/conflicting
+completion, cancelled execution, prepared-secret preservation across reopen,
+and parallel-parent join promotion. A native SQLite trigger rejects completion:
+no partial result or downstream promotion is committed, and a later retry works.
+
+`verify-remote-execution.mjs` starts the built control plane and runner as separate
+processes. A real shell build writes a witness file, followed by a dependent test.
+It loses the initial offer, resumes it, drops a successfully committed completion
+response, kills the control plane with SIGKILL, and restarts on the same SQLite
+file. The saved result is retried and the dependent job executes once. It checks
+final step/job state after another reopen, rejects a forged completion token,
+and verifies witness contents rather than inferring execution from records.
+
+The probe then kills the runner process group after a real shell side effect but
+before result persistence. Restart with the same journal leaves the job uncertain
+and does not repeat the side effect. It checks private journal modes and scans
+journal/process output for fixture secrets. Child processes, SQLite files,
+journals and witness files are removed afterward.
+
+Reproduce after installing the control-plane, runner and existing TestFn workspace
+closure and building shared DB dependencies:
+
+```sh
+npm test --workspace=./cifn/typescript/control-plane
+npm test --workspace=./cifn/typescript/runner
+npm run lint --workspace=./cifn/typescript/control-plane
+npm run lint --workspace=./cifn/typescript/runner
+npm run test:remote --workspace=./cifn/typescript/runner
+npm run test:remote --workspace=./cifn/typescript/control-plane
+```
+
+Validation: 169 control-plane tests and 75 runner tests, package typechecks,
+strict durable/remote configurations with `skipLibCheck:false`, both package
+builds, and the real two-process acceptance probe pass. Existing built startup,
+SQLite dispatch restart and CJS/ESM control-plane consumer probes also pass.
+
+Validation is local Node 20.20.0/native SQLite evidence. The existing runner suite
+also exercises local executor paths; it is not evidence that provider steps are
+supported remotely.
+
+## Remaining original gates
+
+Execution lease expiry/renewal, explicit operator reconciliation/reassignment,
+crash recovery after an unknown subprocess result, durable notification delivery,
+remote step/log streaming, artifact/cache/checkout/TestFn/HostFn/Docker provider
+integration, and step-level secret expressions remain open. Remote shell jobs
+with unsupported providers fail rather than claiming success. Cancellation does
+not terminate a running subprocess. Completion is reported per job, so step
+progress before terminal completion is not durably streamed.
+
+Journal retention/backup and filesystem portability, installed tarball/runtime
+matrices, live FlowFn/SecFn/FileFn/LogFn/SendFn acceptance, distributed load and
+performance targets, production deployment, Python/CLI/dashboard parity and the
+remaining original specification requirements are not completed by this slice.

@@ -0,0 +1,122 @@
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
+import { once } from 'node:events';
+import { createServer } from 'node:http';
+import { mkdtemp, readFile, readdir, rm, stat } from 'node:fs/promises';
+import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';
+import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
+
+const directory = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'cifn-remote-acceptance-'));
+const key = randomBytes(32).toString('base64');
+const apiKey = 'disposable-remote-job-secret';
+const token = 'disposable-remote-registration';
+const children = [];
+let output = '', port = 0, control, proxy, runner, completionBody;
+const stateDirectory = join(directory, 'runner-state');
+const witness = join(directory, 'witness');
+const delay = ms => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
+async function until(check, label, timeout = 20000) {
+  const deadline = Date.now() + timeout;
+  while (Date.now() < deadline) { const value = await check(); if (value) return value; await delay(50); }
+  throw new Error(`Timed out: ${label}`);
+}
+function child(script, env, detached = false) {
+  const processChild = spawn(process.execPath, [script], { env: { ...process.env, ...env }, detached, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });
+  const exited = once(processChild, 'exit'); children.push({ child: processChild, exited, detached });
+  processChild.stdout.on('data', chunk => { output += chunk; }); processChild.stderr.on('data', chunk => { output += chunk; });
+  return { child: processChild, exited, detached };
+}
+async function stop(value, signal = 'SIGTERM') {
+  if (value.child.exitCode === null && value.child.signalCode === null) {
+    if (value.detached) process.kill(-value.child.pid, signal); else value.child.kill(signal);
+  }
+  await value.exited;
+}
+async function startControl() {
+  const value = child(fileURLToPath(new URL('../dist/server.js', import.meta.url)), {
+    PORT: String(port), CIFN_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN: token, CIFN_API_KEYS: apiKey,
+    CIFN_STORE_ADAPTER: 'sqlite', CIFN_SQLITE_PATH: join(directory, 'state.sqlite'), CIFN_STORE_ENCRYPTION_KEY: key,
+    CIFN_QUEUE_ADAPTER: 'memory', CIFN_ARTIFACTS_ADAPTER: 'memory', CIFN_SECRETS_ADAPTER: 'memory', CIFN_LOGS_ADAPTER: 'memory',
+  });
+  let listened;
+  value.child.stdout.on('data', chunk => { const match = /Control Plane listening on port (\d+)/.exec(String(chunk)); if (match) listened = Number(match[1]); });
+  port = await until(async () => { if (value.child.exitCode !== null) throw new Error('Control plane exited before readiness'); return listened; }, 'control startup');
+  return value;
+}
+async function request(path, body, credential = apiKey) {
+  const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${path}`, { method: body === undefined ? 'GET' : 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${credential}` }, body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });
+  return response;
+}
+async function data(path, body, credential) { const response = await request(path, body, credential); assert.ok(response.ok, `${path}: ${response.status}`); return (await response.json()).data; }
+const quote = value => `'${value.replaceAll("'", "'\\''")}'`;
+const command = (label, sleep = false) => `${quote(process.execPath)} -e ${quote(`const fs=require('fs');if(process.env.CIFN_RUNNER_SECRET||process.env.CIFN_API_KEYS||!process.env.TOKEN)process.exit(23);fs.appendFileSync(${JSON.stringify(witness)},${JSON.stringify(label + '\n')});${sleep ? 'setTimeout(()=>{},10000);' : ''}`)}`;
+try {
+  control = await startControl();
+  const registration = await data('/api/v1/runners/register', { token });
+  let dropped = false;
+  proxy = createServer(async (req, res) => {
+    try {
+      const chunks = []; for await (const chunk of req) chunks.push(chunk);
+      const body = Buffer.concat(chunks);
+      const upstream = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}${req.url}`, { method: req.method, headers: { Authorization: req.headers.authorization ?? '', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });
+      const responseBody = await upstream.text();
+      if (!dropped && req.url.endsWith('/claims/complete') && upstream.ok) {
+        dropped = true; completionBody = JSON.parse(body.toString());
+        await stop(control, 'SIGKILL'); res.destroy(); return;
+      }
+      res.writeHead(upstream.status, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }); res.end(responseBody);
+    } catch { res.destroy(); }
+  });
+  await new Promise(resolve => proxy.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve));
+  const proxyPort = proxy.address().port;
+  const startRunner = () => child(fileURLToPath(new URL('../../runner/dist/server.js', import.meta.url)), {
+    CIFN_CONTROL_PLANE_URL: `http://127.0.0.1:${proxyPort}`, CIFN_RUNNER_ID: registration.runnerId,
+    CIFN_RUNNER_SECRET: registration.runnerSecret, CIFN_RUNNER_STATE_DIR: stateDirectory, CIFN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS: '100',
+    CIFN_API_KEYS: 'must-not-reach-shell',
+  }, true);
+  const input = { trigger: { type: 'workflow_dispatch' }, pipelineSpec: { on: { workflow_dispatch: {} }, env: { TOKEN: '${{ secrets.CIFN_API_KEYS }}' }, jobs: {
+    build: { 'runs-on': 'default', steps: [{ run: command('build') }] },
+    test: { 'runs-on': 'default', needs: ['build'], steps: [{ run: command('test') }] },
+  } } };
+  const run = await data('/api/v1/runs', input);
+  // Lose the initial offer response: authenticated resume must recover this offer.
+  const offered = await data('/api/v1/runners/heartbeat', { runnerId: registration.runnerId }, registration.runnerSecret);
+  assert.equal(offered.job.runId, run.runId);
+  runner = startRunner();
+  await until(async () => dropped && control.child.signalCode !== null, 'committed completion response loss');
+  assert.equal(await readFile(witness, 'utf8'), 'build\n');
+  control = await startControl();
+  await until(async () => (await data(`/api/v1/runs/${run.runId}`)).status === 'success', 'DAG completion after restart');
+  assert.equal(await readFile(witness, 'utf8'), 'build\ntest\n');
+  const repeat = await request('/api/v1/runners/claims/complete', completionBody, registration.runnerSecret);
+  assert.equal(repeat.status, 200);
+  assert.equal((await request('/api/v1/runners/claims/complete', { ...completionBody, claimToken: 'wrong' }, registration.runnerSecret)).status, 409);
+  const final = await data(`/api/v1/runs/${run.runId}`);
+  assert.ok(final.jobs.every(job => job.status === 'success' && job.steps.every(step => step.status === 'success')));
+  await stop(runner); await stop(control); control = await startControl();
+  assert.deepEqual(await data(`/api/v1/runs/${run.runId}`), final);
+  // Kill a real subprocess after its side effect but before result persistence.
+  const uncertain = await data('/api/v1/runs', { ...input, pipelineSpec: { ...input.pipelineSpec, jobs: { uncertain: { 'runs-on': 'default', steps: [{ run: command('uncertain', true) }] } } } });
+  runner = startRunner();
+  await until(async () => (await readFile(witness, 'utf8')).includes('uncertain'), 'real started execution');
+  await stop(runner, 'SIGKILL'); runner = startRunner();
+  await delay(1200);
+  assert.equal(await readFile(witness, 'utf8'), 'build\ntest\nuncertain\n');
+  assert.equal((await data(`/api/v1/runs/${uncertain.runId}`)).status, 'running');
+  assert.ok(output.includes('automatic replay refused'));
+  await stop(runner); await stop(control);
+  assert.equal((await stat(stateDirectory)).mode & 0o777, 0o700);
+  for (const name of await readdir(stateDirectory)) {
+    const bytes = await readFile(join(stateDirectory, name));
+    assert.equal((await stat(join(stateDirectory, name))).mode & 0o777, 0o600);
+    for (const value of [apiKey, registration.runnerSecret, token, key]) assert.equal(bytes.includes(Buffer.from(value)), false, 'Journal must not contain raw job/provider credentials');
+  }
+  for (const value of [apiKey, registration.runnerSecret, token, key]) assert.equal(output.includes(value), false, 'Child output must not contain credentials');
+  console.log('Remote shell DAG passed: real side effects, lost offer/completion recovery, SQLite restart, idempotent completion, and uncertain execution refusal');
+} finally {
+  for (const value of children) await stop(value, 'SIGKILL');
+  if (proxy) { proxy.closeAllConnections(); await new Promise(resolve => proxy.close(resolve)); }
+  await rm(directory, { recursive: true, force: true });
+}

+import type { Hono } from 'hono';
+import type { ControlPlaneStore } from '../store/store.js';
+import type { DatabaseStore } from '../store/database-store.js';
+import { compareSecretHash } from '../runners/crypto.js';
+import { readJsonBody, PayloadTooLargeError } from './body.js';
+import { ClaimConflictError, validateCompletion, type ClaimIdentity } from '../dispatch/types.js';
+import { success, error } from './envelope.js';
+
+export function registerClaimRoutes(api: Hono, store: ControlPlaneStore): void {
+  for (const action of ['resume', 'ack', 'complete'] as const) {
+    api.post(`/runners/claims/${action}`, async c => {
+      let body: Record<string, unknown>;
+      try { body = await readJsonBody(c.req.raw); }
+      catch (cause) { return c.json(error('BAD_REQUEST', 'Invalid claim request'), cause instanceof PayloadTooLargeError ? 413 : 400); }
+      const bearer = c.req.header('Authorization');
+      if (typeof body.runnerId !== 'string' || !bearer?.startsWith('Bearer ')) return c.json(error('UNAUTHORIZED', 'Runner authentication required'), 401);
+      const runner = await store.getRunner(body.runnerId);
+      if (!runner || !compareSecretHash(bearer.slice(7), runner.secretHash)) return c.json(error('UNAUTHORIZED', 'Invalid runner authentication'), 401);
+      const durable = store as DatabaseStore;
+      if (typeof durable.completeDispatch !== 'function') return c.json(error('UNAVAILABLE', 'Durable claim protocol unavailable'), 503);
+      try {
+        if (action === 'resume') {
+          if (body.cursor !== undefined && typeof body.cursor !== 'string') return c.json(error('BAD_REQUEST', 'Invalid cursor'), 400);
+          return c.json(success(await durable.listRunnerClaims(runner.id, body.cursor as string | undefined)));
+        }
+        for (const field of ['runId', 'dispatchId', 'claimToken', 'executionId']) {
+          if (typeof body[field] !== 'string' || !body[field] || (body[field] as string).length > 512) return c.json(error('BAD_REQUEST', 'Invalid claim identity'), 400);
+        }
+        const identity: ClaimIdentity = { runId: body.runId as string, dispatchId: body.dispatchId as string, claimToken: body.claimToken as string, executionId: body.executionId as string, runnerId: runner.id };
+        if (action === 'ack') { await durable.acknowledgeDispatch(identity); return c.json(success({ acknowledged: true })); }
+        if (!validateCompletion(body.result)) return c.json(error('BAD_REQUEST', 'Invalid terminal job result'), 400);
+        return c.json(success(await durable.completeDispatch(identity, body.result)));
+      } catch (cause) {
+        if (cause instanceof ClaimConflictError) return c.json(error('CLAIM_CONFLICT', cause.message), 409);
+        return c.json(error('UNAVAILABLE', 'Durable claim operation failed'), 503);
+      }
+    });
+  }
+}

+import { registerClaimRoutes } from './claims.js';
 import { prepareRun, acceptRun } from '../dispatch/prepare.js';
 import { isDispatchStore } from '../dispatch/types.js';
 import { DispatchPublisher } from '../dispatch/publisher.js';
@@ -75,7 +76,7 @@ export function createApp<TStore extends ControlPlaneStore = MemoryStore>(option
   // Apply Auth Middleware to all /api/v1 routes

+import { mkdirSync, chmodSync, openSync, closeSync, writeFileSync, fsyncSync, renameSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, existsSync, linkSync, unlinkSync } from 'node:fs';
+import { join } from 'node:path';
+import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
+import type { ClaimIdentity, JobCompletion } from '@cifn/control-plane';
+
+export interface ClaimJournalEntry extends ClaimIdentity {
+  version: 1;
+  phase: 'prepared' | 'started' | 'completed' | 'finished' | 'reconciliation';
+  result?: JobCompletion;
+}
+/** Contains identity/results only; never stores job payload, environment, or logs. */
+export class ClaimJournal {
+  constructor(private directory: string) { mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 }); chmodSync(directory, 0o700); }
+  private path(dispatchId: string): string { return join(this.directory, createHash('sha256').update(dispatchId).digest('hex')); }
+  private syncDirectory(): void { const fd = openSync(this.directory, 'r'); try { fsyncSync(fd); } finally { closeSync(fd); } }
+  get(dispatchId: string): ClaimJournalEntry | undefined {
+    const path = this.path(dispatchId) + '.json';
+    return existsSync(path) ? this.read(path) : undefined;
+  }
+  private read(path: string): ClaimJournalEntry {
+    const value = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')) as ClaimJournalEntry;
+    if (value.version !== 1 || typeof value.dispatchId !== 'string' || typeof value.executionId !== 'string' || !['prepared', 'started', 'completed', 'finished', 'reconciliation'].includes(value.phase)) throw new Error('Claim journal needs explicit repair');
+    return value;
+  }
+  list(): ClaimJournalEntry[] { return readdirSync(this.directory).filter(name => name.endsWith('.json')).map(name => this.read(join(this.directory, name))); }
+  save(entry: ClaimJournalEntry, createOnly = false): ClaimJournalEntry {
+    const path = this.path(entry.dispatchId) + '.json';
+    const temporary = path + '.' + randomUUID() + '.tmp';
+    const fd = openSync(temporary, 'wx', 0o600);
+    try { writeFileSync(fd, JSON.stringify(entry)); fsyncSync(fd); } finally { closeSync(fd); }
+    try {
+      if (createOnly) {
+        try { linkSync(temporary, path); }
+        catch (cause) { if ((cause as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'EEXIST') throw cause; }
+        unlinkSync(temporary);
+      } else renameSync(temporary, path);
+      this.syncDirectory();
+      return this.read(path);
+    } finally { if (existsSync(temporary)) unlinkSync(temporary); }
+  }
+  hasStarted(dispatchId: string): boolean { return existsSync(this.path(dispatchId) + '.started'); }
+  markStarted(entry: ClaimJournalEntry): boolean {
+    let fd: number;
+    try { fd = openSync(this.path(entry.dispatchId) + '.started', 'wx', 0o600); }
+    catch (cause) { if ((cause as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EEXIST') return false; throw cause; }
+    try { writeFileSync(fd, entry.executionId); fsyncSync(fd); } finally { closeSync(fd); }
+    this.syncDirectory();
+    this.save({ ...entry, phase: 'started' });
+    return true;
+  }
+}

+import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

+describe('durable runner journal', () => {
+  it('preserves initial execution ownership, private modes and exclusive started markers across reopen', () => {
+    const path = directory(); let journal = new ClaimJournal(path);
+    const entry = { version: 1 as const, phase: 'prepared' as const, runnerId: 'runner', runId: 'run', dispatchId: 'dispatch', claimToken: 'claim', executionId: 'owner' };
+    expect(journal.save(entry, true)).toEqual(entry);
+    expect(journal.save({ ...entry, executionId: 'competitor' }, true)).toEqual(entry);
+    expect(journal.markStarted(entry)).toBe(true);
+    expect(journal.markStarted(entry)).toBe(false);
+    journal = new ClaimJournal(path);
+    expect(journal.hasStarted(entry.dispatchId)).toBe(true);
+    expect(journal.get(entry.dispatchId)?.phase).toBe('started');
+    expect(statSync(path).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o700);
+    for (const name of readdirSync(path)) expect(statSync(join(path, name)).mode & 0o777).toBe(0o600);
+    const result = { status: 'success' as const, steps: [{ stepKey: 'step-0', status: 'success' as const }] };
+    journal.save({ ...entry, phase: 'completed', result });
+    expect(new ClaimJournal(path).list()).toEqual([{ ...entry, phase: 'completed', result }]);
+    expect(readdirSync(path).some(name => name.endsWith('.tmp'))).toBe(false);
+    expect(readFileSync(join(path, readdirSync(path).find(name => name.endsWith('.json'))!), 'utf8')).not.toContain('env');

+export interface RemoteRunnerOptions { baseUrl: string; runnerId: string; runnerSecret: string; stateDirectory: string; fetch?: typeof fetch }
+interface ResumableClaim { payload?: JobPayload; runId: string; dispatchId: string; claimToken: string; executionId?: string; reconciliationRequired: boolean }
+
+/** Reuses the real shell executor. The memory projection is scratch state only. */
+export async function executeRemoteShellJob(payload: JobPayload): Promise<JobCompletion> {
+  const failed = (): JobCompletion => ({ status: 'failure', steps: payload.jobSpec.steps.map((_, index) => ({ stepKey: `step-${index}`, status: index === 0 ? 'failure' : 'skipped' })) });
+  if (payload.jobSpec.image || payload.jobSpec.steps.some(step => !('run' in step))) {
+    console.error('Remote job requires an unsupported executor/provider'); return failed();
+  }
+  const store = new MemoryStore(); const queue = new MemoryQueueClient();
+  // Prepared environments are authoritative snapshots; do not interpolate them twice.
+  const jobSpec = { ...payload.jobSpec, needs: [], env: undefined };
+  const spec: PipelineSpec = { on: { workflow_dispatch: {} }, jobs: { [payload.jobKey]: jobSpec } };
+  const run = store.createRun({ pipelineSpec: spec, pipelineRef: payload.pipelineRef, trigger: { type: (payload.trigger?.type ?? 'workflow_dispatch') as 'workflow_dispatch', payload: payload.trigger?.payload } });
+  await queue.enqueue(DEFAULT_QUEUE_NAME, { ...payload, runId: run.id, jobSpec });
+  const runner = new Runner({ executionEnv: { PATH: process.env.PATH, LANG: process.env.LANG, TMPDIR: process.env.TMPDIR }, store, queue, logClient: new MemoryLogFnClient(), labels: [jobSpec['runs-on']],
+    pipelineSpecs: new Map([[run.id, spec]]), secretValues: new Map([[run.id, Object.values(payload.env ?? {}).filter(Boolean)]]) });
+  try { await runner.processNextJob(); } catch { return failed(); }
+  const result = store.getRun(run.id)!.jobs[0];
+  const status = ['success', 'failure', 'skipped'].includes(result.status) ? result.status as JobCompletion['status'] : 'failure';
+  const steps: JobCompletion['steps'] = result.steps.map(step => ({ stepKey: step.stepKey, status: ['success', 'failure', 'skipped'].includes(step.status) ? step.status as JobCompletion['status'] : 'skipped' }));

+
+class RunnerProtocolError extends Error { constructor(readonly status: number) { super(`Runner protocol request failed (${status})`); } }
+
+export class RemoteRunner {
+  private journal: ClaimJournal;
+  private fetcher: typeof fetch;
+  private reportedUncertain = new Set<string>();
+  constructor(private options: RemoteRunnerOptions) { this.journal = new ClaimJournal(options.stateDirectory); this.fetcher = options.fetch ?? fetch; }
+  private async request<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<T> {
+    const response = await this.fetcher(this.options.baseUrl + path, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${this.options.runnerSecret}` }, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) });
+    if (!response.ok) throw new RunnerProtocolError(response.status);
+    const envelope = await response.json() as { ok: boolean; data: T };
+    if (!envelope.ok) throw new Error('Runner protocol request failed');
+    return envelope.data;
+  }
+  private async finish(entry: ClaimJournalEntry): Promise<void> {
+    try {
+      await this.request('/api/v1/runners/claims/complete', { ...entry, runnerId: this.options.runnerId, result: entry.result });
+      this.journal.save({ ...entry, phase: 'finished' });
+    } catch (cause) {
+      if (!(cause instanceof RunnerProtocolError) || (cause.status !== 409 && cause.status !== 400)) throw cause;
+      this.journal.save({ ...entry, phase: 'reconciliation' });
+      console.error('CiFn completion requires reconciliation; conflicting result retained');
+    }
+  }
+  private async handle(claim: ResumableClaim): Promise<boolean> {
+    if (claim.reconciliationRequired || !claim.payload) return false;
+    let entry = this.journal.get(claim.dispatchId);
+    if (!entry) {
+      if (claim.executionId) return false; // Acknowledged elsewhere: never invent execution ownership.
+      entry = this.journal.save({ version: 1, phase: 'prepared', runnerId: this.options.runnerId, runId: claim.runId, dispatchId: claim.dispatchId, claimToken: claim.claimToken, executionId: randomUUID() }, true);
+    }
+    if (entry.runnerId !== this.options.runnerId || (claim.executionId && claim.executionId !== entry.executionId)) return false;
+    if (entry.phase === 'finished' || entry.phase === 'reconciliation') return false;
+    if (entry.phase === 'completed') { await this.finish(entry); return true; }
+    if (entry.phase === 'started' || this.journal.hasStarted(entry.dispatchId)) {
+      if (!this.reportedUncertain.has(entry.dispatchId)) { console.error('CiFn execution requires reconciliation; automatic replay refused'); this.reportedUncertain.add(entry.dispatchId); }
+      return false;
+    }
+    await this.request('/api/v1/runners/claims/ack', entry);
+    if (!this.journal.markStarted(entry)) return false;
+    const result = await executeRemoteShellJob(claim.payload);
+    const completed = { ...entry, phase: 'completed' as const, result };
+    this.journal.save(completed);
+    await this.finish(completed);
+    return true;
+  }
+  async tick(): Promise<number> {
+    let processed = 0;
+    for (const entry of this.journal.list()) {
+      if (entry.runnerId === this.options.runnerId && entry.phase === 'completed') { await this.finish(entry); processed++; }
+    }
+    let cursor: string | undefined;
+    do {
+      const page: { claims: ResumableClaim[]; nextCursor?: string } = await this.request('/api/v1/runners/claims/resume', { runnerId: this.options.runnerId, cursor });
+      for (const claim of page.claims) if (await this.handle(claim)) processed++;
+      cursor = page.nextCursor;
+    } while (cursor);
+    const heartbeat = await this.request<{ job: JobPayload | null }>('/api/v1/runners/heartbeat', { runnerId: this.options.runnerId });
+    if (heartbeat.job?.dispatchId && heartbeat.job.claimToken) {
+      if (await this.handle({ payload: heartbeat.job, runId: heartbeat.job.runId, dispatchId: heartbeat.job.dispatchId, claimToken: heartbeat.job.claimToken, reconciliationRequired: false })) processed++;
+    }
+    return processed;
+  }
+}

+# CiFn durable remote shell execution checkpoint
+
+2026-10-20. Adds a functioning remote shell runner to the durable control plane.
+It supersedes the root-only/no-completion limits in the earlier dispatch
+checkpoint for newly prepared runs. Production readiness remains incomplete.
+
+## Protocol and durable state
+
+All jobs now have an encrypted prepared payload captured at run acceptance.
+Root intents start ready; dependent intents start blocked. Their environment and
+secret snapshot is retained rather than reconstructed or re-resolved when a
+predecessor completes.
+
+The existing authenticated heartbeat offers a durable claim. Three bounded JSON
+endpoints use the registered runner secret, not an application API key:
+
+- `POST /api/v1/runners/claims/resume`: `runnerId`, optional pagination cursor.
+  Returns only that runner's outstanding claims and their prepared payloads.
+- `POST /api/v1/runners/claims/ack`: `runnerId`, `runId`, `dispatchId`,
+  `claimToken`, `executionId`. CAS binds an execution identity before work starts.
+  Repeating the same acknowledgement is safe; competing identities conflict.
+- `POST /api/v1/runners/claims/complete`: the same identity plus `result` with a
+  terminal job status and the exact ordered step keys/terminal statuses.
+
+Completion requires the runner binding, claim token and acknowledged execution
+identity. Invalid authentication returns 401, malformed shape 400, stale or
+conflicting identity/result 409, and a storage failure 503. Server-observed
+completion timestamps are assigned internally. A canonical result digest makes
+identical retries return the same `{accepted:true}` receipt without applying a
+second transition; a conflicting result is rejected.
+
+One run-row CAS commits completion, step/job statuses, dependent-intent promotion
+and the resulting run status. An already ready/claimed/completed intent cannot
+be scheduled again. Concurrent parent completions can release a join only once.
+Failed dependencies skip blocked descendants; independent branches may finish.
+A run becomes terminal only when all jobs are terminal. Cancelled runs reject
+new execution acknowledgements and completions that were not already committed.
+Notifications are not made durable by this transition.
+
+The payload's `dispatchProtocolVersion:2` marks fully prepared runs. Earlier
+record-only or root-only payloads remain readable but are not automatically
+published/claimed by this execution protocol. Old claims without protocol
+metadata are reconciliation-only. There is no automatic migration or unsafe
+secret re-resolution for historical records; reconcile them explicitly before
+creating replacement work.
+
+## Runner lifecycle and secret handling
+
+The built runner requires `CIFN_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, `CIFN_RUNNER_ID`,
+`CIFN_RUNNER_SECRET` and an explicit persistent `CIFN_RUNNER_STATE_DIR`.
+`CIFN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` defaults to 1000 (minimum 10). The control plane must use
+the durable SQLite store for these endpoints. MemoryStore remains available for
+local execution, not remote durability.
+
+The runner reuses the existing Runner and shell executor with an ephemeral
+per-job projection. That projection drives actual subprocess execution and
+collects results; it is not the durable authority. Only shell `run` steps are
+supported by this remote checkpoint. Image/container jobs and provider `uses`
+steps fail explicitly. Existing local execution/provider paths remain available
+and separately tested.
+
+Before acknowledging a claim, the runner saves only identity/execution metadata
+in its journal. It fsyncs an exclusive started marker before invoking the shell,
+then durably saves terminal statuses before sending completion. Journal files
+use mode 0600, the directory mode 0700, atomic replacement and directory fsync.
+The journal contains no raw job environment, commands, log output, provider
+credentials or runner secret. It retains scoped claim/execution tokens and
+terminal statuses. Resume re-fetches payloads through runner authentication.
+
+On restart:
+
+- Unacknowledged offers and prepared journal entries may be resumed.
+- A saved completed result is resent, never re-executed. A permanent conflict or
+  invalid result is retained in reconciliation state without blocking later jobs.
+- A started marker without a saved result is uncertain. The runner emits a
+  generic reconciliation diagnostic and refuses automatic re-execution.
+- An execution acknowledged elsewhere cannot be adopted with a new identity.
+
+The exclusive started marker also prevents two local processes using one journal
+from spawning the same execution. This protects against duplicate execution
+caused by protocol/journal retries; it does not claim exactly-once external side
+effects or recover an unknown result after a process/host loss.
+
+Full-job logging was removed. Shell jobs receive prepared job variables plus a
+small base environment (PATH/LANG/TMPDIR), not the runner's control-plane
+credentials. Results saved/reported by this path contain statuses only, so raw
+stdout/stderr and secret values cannot enter the journal. Existing executor
+redaction is retained for its in-memory logs. This is not an OS/container sandbox.
+
+## Validation
+
+Real SQLite protocol tests exercise owner/runner/token binding, acknowledgement
+retries, competing execution owners, wrong step results, duplicate/conflicting
+completion, cancelled execution, prepared-secret preservation across reopen,
+and parallel-parent join promotion. A native SQLite trigger rejects completion:
+no partial result or downstream promotion is committed, and a later retry works.
+
+`verify-remote-execution.mjs` starts the built control plane and runner as separate
+processes. A real shell build writes a witness file, followed by a dependent test.
+It loses the initial offer, resumes it, drops a successfully committed completion
+response, kills the control plane with SIGKILL, and restarts on the same SQLite
+file. The saved result is retried and the dependent job executes once. It checks
+final step/job state after another reopen, rejects a forged completion token,
+and verifies witness contents rather than inferring execution from records.
+
+The probe then kills the runner process group after a real shell side effect but
+before result persistence. Restart with the same journal leaves the job uncertain
+and does not repeat the side effect. It checks private journal modes and scans
+journal/process output for fixture secrets. Child processes, SQLite files,
+journals and witness files are removed afterward.
+
+Reproduce after installing the control-plane, runner and existing TestFn workspace
+closure and building shared DB dependencies:
+
+```sh
+npm test --workspace=./cifn/typescript/control-plane
+npm test --workspace=./cifn/typescript/runner
+npm run lint --workspace=./cifn/typescript/control-plane
+npm run lint --workspace=./cifn/typescript/runner
+npm run test:remote --workspace=./cifn/typescript/runner
+npm run test:remote --workspace=./cifn/typescript/control-plane
+```
+
+Validation: 169 control-plane tests and 75 runner tests, package typechecks,
+strict durable/remote configurations with `skipLibCheck:false`, both package
+builds, and the real two-process acceptance probe pass. Existing built startup,
+SQLite dispatch restart and CJS/ESM control-plane consumer probes also pass.
+
+Validation is local Node 20.20.0/native SQLite evidence. The existing runner suite
+also exercises local executor paths; it is not evidence that provider steps are
+supported remotely.
+
+## Remaining original gates
+
+Execution lease expiry/renewal, explicit operator reconciliation/reassignment,
+crash recovery after an unknown subprocess result, durable notification delivery,
+remote step/log streaming, artifact/cache/checkout/TestFn/HostFn/Docker provider
+integration, and step-level secret expressions remain open. Remote shell jobs
+with unsupported providers fail rather than claiming success. Cancellation does
+not terminate a running subprocess. Completion is reported per job, so step
+progress before terminal completion is not durably streamed.
+
+Journal retention/backup and filesystem portability, installed tarball/runtime
+matrices, live FlowFn/SecFn/FileFn/LogFn/SendFn acceptance, distributed load and
+performance targets, production deployment, Python/CLI/dashboard parity and the
+remaining original specification requirements are not completed by this slice.

+export async function executeRemoteShellJob(payload: JobPayload): Promise<JobCompletion> {

# Requested checkpoint playback video

`checkpoint create --include-video` and MCP `probefn_checkpoint_create` with
`includeVideo: true` record the requested checkpoint playback as WebM. Recording
starts when that command creates its browser page and ends after screenshot,
DOM, accessibility, layout and optional style capture. Its duration follows that
navigation and capture operation; there is no fixed-duration recording window.
The runtime currently opens a fresh browser playback for each command, so this
file does not contain previous actions or continuous historical session footage.
Unrequested checkpoints do not enable video recording.

The recording page closes before Playwright finalizes and saves the video. Its
context remains alive long enough to persist browser storage state, then normal
browser cleanup closes it. The artifact store writes the completed nonempty file
under the checkpoint directory as `video.webm`, and its SHA-256 is included in the
checkpoint manifest. Video capture or persistence failure rejects the checkpoint
with `E_CHECKPOINT_CAPTURE_FAILED`; the manifest is committed only after required
artifacts exist. Temporary recording files are removed on browser cleanup.

Local verification uses actual Chromium to capture and decode a finalized WebM,
check its manifest hash, exercise finalization failure without a committed
manifest, and verify temporary recording cleanup. A separate actual Chromium
check exercises both CLI and MCP argument propagation, successful playback
cleanup and persisted video references. Existing browser lifecycle and core
checkpoint tests also pass. This is not Firefox/WebKit video or hosted deployment
evidence.
EOF

# TestFn V0 Specification

> Comprehensive self-hosted testing platform for developers

## Overview

TestFn is a developer-first testing solution that combines test execution, analytics, and visual testing into a single self-hosted platform. It builds on the super-functions ecosystem, reusing proven patterns from searchfn and @superfunctions/db.

**Version**: 0.1.0
**Target Release**: Q1 2026
**Status**: Specification

## Core Philosophy

- **Self-hosted first**: No external dependencies or cloud services
- **Developer experience**: Simple SDK, works locally, minimal configuration
- **Comprehensive**: Unit, integration, E2E, and visual testing in one tool
- **Performance**: Fast execution, efficient storage, real-time analytics
- **Ecosystem integration**: Leverages super-functions infrastructure

## Architecture

```
testfn/
├── ts-sdk/
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── core/           # Test orchestration & execution
│   │   ├── storage/        # Results persistence layer
│   │   ├── analytics/      # Metrics, trends, flaky detection
│   │   ├── reporters/      # Output formatters (HTML, JSON, console)
│   │   ├── visual/         # Screenshot comparison & diffing
│   │   └── integrations/   # Framework adapters (Vitest, Playwright)
│   └── examples/
├── py-sdk/                 # Python SDK (future)
└── dashboard/              # Static HTML viewer
```

## V0 Features

### 1. Test Execution & Orchestration

#### Test Runner Core
**Priority**: P0 (Critical)

Provides the foundation for running tests across different frameworks.

**Capabilities**:
- Framework detection and adapter loading
- Test discovery and filtering
- Parallel execution with worker pool
- Result collection and aggregation
- Error handling and retry logic

**API Design**:
```typescript
interface TestFnConfig {
  framework: 'vitest' | 'playwright' | 'jest' | 'puppeteer';
  testPattern?: string | string[];
  parallel?: number | 'auto';
  timeout?: number;
  retries?: number;
  env?: Record<string, string>;
  browsers?: ('chromium' | 'firefox' | 'webkit')[];
  storage?: StorageConfig;
  onProgress?: (progress: TestProgress) => void;
  onComplete?: (results: TestResults) => void;
}

interface StorageConfig {
  type: 'indexeddb' | 'file' | 'db';
  dbName?: string;
  adapter?: Adapter;
  retentionDays?: number;
}

const runner = testFn({
  framework: 'playwright',
  testPattern: './tests/**/*.spec.ts',
  parallel: 4,
  browsers: ['chromium', 'firefox'],

# TestFn V0 Specification

> Comprehensive self-hosted testing platform for developers

## Overview

TestFn is a developer-first testing solution that combines test execution, analytics, and visual testing into a single self-hosted platform. It builds on the super-functions ecosystem, reusing proven patterns from searchfn and @superfunctions/db.

**Version**: 0.1.0
**Target Release**: Q1 2026
**Status**: Specification

## Core Philosophy

- **Self-hosted first**: No external dependencies or cloud services
- **Developer experience**: Simple SDK, works locally, minimal configuration
- **Comprehensive**: Unit, integration, E2E, and visual testing in one tool
- **Performance**: Fast execution, efficient storage, real-time analytics
- **Ecosystem integration**: Leverages super-functions infrastructure

## Architecture

```
testfn/
├── ts-sdk/
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── core/           # Test orchestration & execution
│   │   ├── storage/        # Results persistence layer
│   │   ├── analytics/      # Metrics, trends, flaky detection
│   │   ├── reporters/      # Output formatters (HTML, JSON, console)
│   │   ├── visual/         # Screenshot comparison & diffing
│   │   └── integrations/   # Framework adapters (Vitest, Playwright)
│   └── examples/
├── py-sdk/                 # Python SDK (future)
└── dashboard/              # Static HTML viewer
```

## V0 Features

### 1. Test Execution & Orchestration

#### Test Runner Core
**Priority**: P0 (Critical)

Provides the foundation for running tests across different frameworks.

**Capabilities**:
- Framework detection and adapter loading
- Test discovery and filtering
- Parallel execution with worker pool
- Result collection and aggregation
- Error handling and retry logic

**API Design**:
```typescript
interface TestFnConfig {
  framework: 'vitest' | 'playwright' | 'jest' | 'puppeteer';
  testPattern?: string | string[];
  parallel?: number | 'auto';
  timeout?: number;
  retries?: number;
  env?: Record<string, string>;
  browsers?: ('chromium' | 'firefox' | 'webkit')[];
  storage?: StorageConfig;
  onProgress?: (progress: TestProgress) => void;
  onComplete?: (results: TestResults) => void;
}

interface StorageConfig {
  type: 'indexeddb' | 'file' | 'db';
  dbName?: string;
  adapter?: Adapter;
  retentionDays?: number;
}

const runner = testFn({
  framework: 'playwright',
  testPattern: './tests/**/*.spec.ts',
  parallel: 4,
  browsers: ['chromium', 'firefox'],
  storage: {
    type: 'indexeddb',
    dbName: 'testfn-results'
  },
  onProgress: (progress) => {
    console.log(`${progress.completed}/${progress.total}`);
  }
});

await runner.run();
```

# Framework subprocess ownership checkpoint

The original execution/cancellation contract now waits for the owned POSIX
process group to disappear before returning from a framework process. Previously,
a framework leader could exit successfully while an ignored-stdio descendant
continued running; the caller received exit code zero and ownership ended.

Leader exit and stream closure are observed separately. Residual descendants
receive SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after one second if necessary. Group disappearance
is checked for up to five additional seconds; stream drain has a separate
one-second bound. A normal framework exit with surviving descendants is reported
as failure. Cancellation, execution timeout and output overflow use the same
owned-group cleanup. Permission errors or an unconfirmed termination reject the
operation instead of claiming that execution stopped. Cleanup finishes before
its promise settles. No process identity is recovered from persistent state.

Actual local macOS subprocess tests exercise SIGTERM-resistant descendants with
ignored and explicitly closed stdout/stderr, normal-exit orphan cleanup,
cancellation, timeout, and an unrelated sentinel that remains alive. A permission
failure injected only at the group signal boundary verifies rejection while the
real descendant is still running; the test then restores signalling and removes

Key classes/modules:
- `CatchFn`: main facade; holds watchfn client, config, reporters.
- `ReporterWidget`: overlay UI; collects form inputs, captures screenshot, allows annotation via `drawfn`.
- `ContextCollectors`: console log buffer, network interceptor (wraps fetch/XMLHttpRequest), device/env collectors; must be opt-in and size-capped.
- `Uploader`: (optional) uploads large attachments to watchfn file channel or provided endpoint; falls back to dataURL for small images.

## UI/UX (Reporter Widget)
- Trigger: `catcher.openReporter()` or global hotkey (configurable) or floating button (opt-in).
- Flow:
  1) Capture screenshot of current viewport (html2canvas or browser capture API).
  2) Annotate using `drawfn` overlay (arrows, boxes, text, blur).
  3) Form: title (required), description, steps, severity, tags, checkbox to include console/network logs.
  4) Submit -> calls `captureBug`; shows success + issue link if integration enabled.
- Accessibility: focus trap, keyboard navigation, prefers-reduced-motion respect.

## Transport & Ingestion
- Reuse `watchfn` browser client; add `bug_report` event type.
- Batching/resilience: leverage `watchfn` batcher; retries with backoff; drop on exceeding size cap.
- Size limits: enforce configurable max payload; compress console/network logs (truncate to last N).
- Security: API key via `watchfn` auth; CORS same as watchfn.

## Issue Sync (GitHub/Linear)
- Client includes optional `integration` hint.
- Server-side (via `botfn` service or lightweight handler) creates issue and writes back `issueId/issueUrl`.
- Status sync: when issue closes, propagate to watchfn/botfn state (future v1.1).

## Session Replay (v1.1)
- Optional plugin that records DOM mutations + input events with redaction; stores `replayId` via `watchfn`.
- Bug reports include `replayId` for playback in dashboard.

## Privacy & Redaction
- `beforeSend(event)` hook to drop or scrub fields.
# CatchFn canonical WatchFn delivery checkpoint

2026-10-20 UTC. CatchFn now accepts `watch: { endpoint, apiKey, ...transportOptions }` and constructs the shared `@watchfn/browser` client with automatic RUM disabled. Explicit bug capture bypasses sampling and DOM availability, preserving the canonical envelope. Existing injected capture clients remain supported. The endpoint path defaults to 64 KiB and rejects configured limits above WatchFn's per-event ingestion ceiling. Larger attachments require upload references.

Capture awaits shared authenticated delivery. Transient statuses/network failures use the existing bounded retry mechanism; authorization failures reject without automatic retry. Failed reports remain queued for explicit `flush()` recovery. Retrying `captureBug()` creates another report, so flush is the retry operation for an already queued report. Delivery is at least once; a successful insert followed by a lost response produces duplicate arrivals with the same report ID. There is no deduplication claim.

The CatchFn branch includes the WatchFn prerequisite and its current shared DB prerequisite; the CatchFn PR is stacked on the WatchFn branch so those changes are not duplicated in its diff. WatchFn validates canonical bug reports before ingestion and persists the unchanged envelope in its normal datastore. The separate flat-report CatchFn service remains available but is not the storage path used by this transport.

Validation:

- CatchFn SDK build/declarations and typecheck pass. All 83 SDK tests pass, including endpoint/authentication mapping without a DOM and payload ceiling validation.
- `scripts/watchfn-acceptance.mjs` exercises built CatchFn and WatchFn through actual loopback HTTP, bearer authentication and shared Kysely/SQLite persistence. It validates transient retry with an unchanged body, canonical report/query fields, final-hook redaction, nonretryable401, lost response duplicates, close/reopen persistence and dropped-table503 failure. Temporary servers, files and connections are removed.
- The native command used Node20.20.0 and `CATCHFN_WATCH_CORE` pointing to the built WatchFn prerequisite checkout. WatchFn was rebuilt after merging the latest shared DB prerequisites; its147 coretests passed. CatchFn's local full WatchFn build initially lacked optional framework adapter dependencies; the explicit built-prerequisite path avoids implying those framework builds passed in the CatchFn checkout. Browser transport and CatchFn builds ran in the CatchFn checkout itself.
- Native acceptance requires built shared DB, Kysely and a working better-sqlite3 binding. Build WatchFn in a checkout with its framework adapter prerequisites, or set `CATCHFN_WATCH_CORE` to that build's `index.mjs`. Run `node catchfn/typescript/scripts/watchfn-acceptance.mjs` from the repository root. Generated artifacts are excluded; no ignore changes are needed.

Remaining original gates include deduplication/atomic ingestion, application indexes and retention overrides, attachment channel provisioning, BotFn issue linking, Python transport parity/historical Python support, browser-hosted CORS/unload/offline acceptance, performance/accessibility and deployment. This is partial progress, not full readiness or a release.

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

### Examples

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring

- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter

- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)
- Function memoization
- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`
4. Create `.conduct/` for artifacts
5. Add to workspace in root `package.json`
6. Package name: `{functionname}` (not scoped unless multi-package)

### Adding a Shared Package

1. Create in `packages/{name}/`
2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)
4. Update dependent packages

### Creating Artifacts

1. Function-specific: `{function}/.conduct/{artifact}.md`
2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

### Working with Turbo

```bash
# Run task across all packages
turbo run build
turbo run test

# Run for specific package
turbo run build --filter=authfn

# Run with dependencies
turbo run build --filter=authfn...

```

## 🚀 Best Practices

### Super functions ecosystem (Very important)

- Reuse shared packages from `packages/` folder like http abstraction, db abstraction, etc.
- Never duplicate shared code like http adapters, db abstractions, etc.
- Don't reexport http-adapters etc - end consumers of the core function package will use the adapters directly. Refer `authfn` implementation for usage of core http router, core db, http adapters and db interface usage.
- Function packages that accept a `@superfunctions/db` `Adapter` must wrap the incoming adapter internally with their own schema, for example `wrapWithSchema(config.database, getSchema(...))`, before passing it to services/storage. Do not require app consumers to pass `adapterSchema` to `drizzleAdapter`, `kyselyAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or `memoryAdapter`; `adapterSchema` is a deprecated compatibility escape hatch for direct app-level adapter use.

### Code Organization

- Keep shared code in `packages/`
- Keep function-specific code in `{function}/`
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Provide Python SDKs for backend-focused functions

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

### Examples

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

## 🔧 Development Workflow

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

### DrawFn

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

### PlugFn

- Self-hosted integration platform
- 75+ provider integrations (GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Stripe)
- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring
- FlexSearch-compatible API
- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

### MailFn

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter
- Raw MIME and attachment evidence, waits, OTP/link extraction, threads, labels, and search
- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition
- Scoped credentials, retention, audit, quotas, and explicitly gated public-platform controls

### CacheFn

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)
- Function memoization
- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`
4. Create `.conduct/` for artifacts
5. Add to workspace in root `package.json`
6. Package name: `{functionname}` (not scoped unless multi-package)

### Adding a Shared Package

1. Create in `packages/{name}/`
2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)
4. Update dependent packages

### Creating Artifacts

1. Function-specific: `{function}/.conduct/{artifact}.md`
2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

### Working with Turbo

```bash
# Run task across all packages
turbo run build
turbo run test

# Run for specific package
turbo run build --filter=authfn

# Run with dependencies
turbo run build --filter=authfn...

# Clear cache
turbo run clean
```

## 📚 Important Files

### Root Configuration

- `package.json` - Workspace and script definitions
- `turbo.json` - Turbo build configuration
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript base config (if exists)

### Package Configuration

- `package.json` - Package metadata, dependencies, scripts
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration
- `vitest.config.ts` - Test configuration
- `pyproject.toml` - Python package configuration

### Documentation

- `README.md` - Package overview and usage
- `SPEC.md` - Technical specification (common in larger functions)
- `.conduct/*.md` - Implementation plans, audits, tasks

## 🔍 Finding Code

### Search Patterns

- **Function implementations**: `{function}/typescript/src/` or `{function}/python/{function}/`
- **Tests**: `__tests__/`, `tests/`, `*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`
- **Types**: `types.ts`, `models.py`, `src/types/`
- **Adapters**: `packages/http-*/`, `packages/python-*/`, `adapters/`
- **Examples**: `examples/`, `{function}/examples/`

### Key Directories

```
superfunctions/
├── {function}/              # Core function packages
│   ├── typescript/          # TS implementation
│   ├── python/              # Python implementation
│   ├── .conduct/            # Artifacts
│   ├── README.md            # Documentation
│   └── SPEC.md              # Specification (if exists)
├── packages/                # Shared packages
│   ├── {name}/              # @superfunctions/{name}
│   └── python-{name}/       # Python shared packages
└── _conduct/                # Root artifacts
```

## 🚀 Best Practices

### Super functions ecosystem (Very important)

- Reuse shared packages from `packages/` folder like http abstraction, db abstraction, etc.
- Never duplicate shared code like http adapters, db abstractions, etc.
- Don't reexport http-adapters etc - end consumers of the core function package will use the adapters directly. Refer `authfn` implementation for usage of core http router, core db, http adapters and db interface usage.
- Function packages that accept a `@superfunctions/db` `Adapter` must wrap the incoming adapter internally with their own schema, for example `wrapWithSchema(config.database, getSchema(...))`, before passing it to services/storage. Do not require app consumers to pass `adapterSchema` to `drizzleAdapter`, `kyselyAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or `memoryAdapter`; `adapterSchema` is a deprecated compatibility escape hatch for direct app-level adapter use.

### Code Organization

- Keep shared code in `packages/`
- Keep function-specific code in `{function}/`
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Provide Python SDKs for backend-focused functions
- Write comprehensive tests

### Documentation

- Update README.md with usage examples
- Create SPEC.md for complex functions
- Document breaking changes
- Keep artifacts in `.conduct/` folders

### Testing

- Use Vitest for TypeScript
- Use pytest for Python
- Maintain high test coverage
- Test adapters separately

### Versioning

- Follow semantic versioning
- Coordinate versions across language SDKs
- Document migration guides for breaking changes

## 🔗 Related Resources

- **Repository**: https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions
- **License**: MIT (most packages) / Apache-2.0 (some packages)
- **Organization**: 21n
- **Contact**: hello@21n.org

## 📝 Notes for AI Agents

1. **Always check both TypeScript and Python** implementations when working on core functions
2. **Respect the naming conventions** - shared packages use `@superfunctions/`, functions use simple names
3. **Create artifacts in `.conduct/` folders**, not in root or arbitrary locations
4. **Avoid nested monorepos** - use subfolders within the main Turbo monorepo
5. **Use Turbo commands** for cross-package operations
6. **Check existing patterns** in similar functions before implementing new features
7. **Maintain consistency** across TypeScript and Python SDKs
8. **Update workspaces** in root `package.json` when adding new packages
9. **Follow existing test patterns** (Vitest for TS, pytest for Python)
10. **Document thoroughly** - this is a developer-focused ecosystem

---

**Last Updated**: 2026-08-10
**Monorepo Version**: 0.1.0
**Package Manager**: npm@10.2.0
**Build Tool**: Turbo v2.0.0

{"cmd":"cat > catchfn/.conduct/browser-delivery-readiness.md <<'EOF'
# Browser report delivery recovery

2026-10-20 UTC. A failed widget submission previously left its canonical report queued in WatchFn, but submitting again prepared another report ID. Delivery failures now expose `CatchFnDeliveryError` with `reportId` and an awaitable `retry()` that reuses the prepared payload. Endpoint retries flush accepted events; a queue-capacity rejection retries enqueueing the same envelope. Injected clients receive the same prepared ID and payload on retry. Successful retry results are retained and concurrent calls share one attempt. Preparation failures remain ordinary errors and do not acquire delivery retry semantics.

The widget locks report fields after delivery failure, displays an unconfirmed-delivery state, and offers Retry same report. Starting a new report is a separate explicit action with a warning that the queued original may still be delivered. Success is shown only after transport acknowledgement. Prepared attachments and beforeSend hooks are not rerun for delivery retries.

## Validation

- All 86 TypeScript SDK tests pass, including actual loopback HTTP repeated failure/recovery, concurrent retry calls, queue-capacity rejection, unchanged report IDs/payloads, and injected-client integration results.
- Typecheck and ESM/CommonJS/declaration builds pass.
- `scripts/browser-delivery-acceptance.mjs` passes in actual installed Chrome against two local origins, WatchFn's real ingestion/query router, and shared Kysely/native SQLite storage. It covers repeated503 failure, locked fields, unchanged canonical payload, bearer authentication, final-hook redaction, browser offline recovery, denied CORS then recovery, accepted persistence followed by response timeout, and explicit creation of a new report while an original is queued.
- The response-timeout case verifies two persisted arrivals with the same report ID after retry. It does not treat matching IDs as datastore deduplication.
- Existing `scripts/watchfn-acceptance.mjs` passes built-package HTTP/SQLite reopen, authentication, retries, canonical query and storage-failure checks. Existing `scripts/browser-acceptance.mjs` passes Chrome and WebKit widget, masking, annotation, consent and focus checks with an injected client.

Reproduce after building CatchFn, WatchFn/shared DB and installing native SQLite plus Chrome:

```sh
CATCHFN_WATCH_CORE=/absolute/path/to/watchfn/typescript/dist/index.mjs node catchfn/typescript/scripts/browser-delivery-acceptance.mjs
```

The local run used the built WatchFn core from the sibling `watchfn-sf-next-readiness` checkout. The script otherwise defaults to this checkout's WatchFn build. Temporary files, native database connections, browser and servers are cleaned up.

## Remaining boundaries

The CORS policy belongs to the hosting server; the acceptance installs an explicit origin allowlist around the real WatchFn router. It does not establish hosted deployment, unload guarantees, persistent offline storage, or network delivery in all browser engines. The queue is in memory, and retries remain at least once. No Python behavior changed.

BotFn issue creation/linking remains open. It needs an authenticated server-side integration at canonical WatchFn bug-report ingestion, durable delivery/duplicate handling and persisted issue-link results. Adding delivery only to the separate flat-report service would not connect the browser's canonical path and is not evidence for this requirement. Retention/index tuning, deduplication, attachment provisioning, Python parity, performance and broader accessibility gates remain open.
EOF

- `beforeAll` prepares a dataset using CacheFn `getOrFetch`.
